source_title: Rare dinosaur skeleton ‘Jodi’ sells for ₹449 crore after fierce bidding war in New York - here's what mak - The Times of India
source_excerpt: A dinosaur skeleton that was expected to sell for around â¹85 crore ended up fetching a whopping â¹449 crore at an auction in New York. The fossil, belonging to Nanotyrannus, a smaller relative of the Tyrannosaurus rex, attracted intense interest from collectors, with six bidders competing to take it home.The skeleton, known as Jodi, was sold by Sotheby's after a 12-minute bidding battle on Tuesday. Bids came in online and over the phone, but the winning offer was eventually made by phone. The buyer's identity has not been disclosed.It's a remarkable price for a fossil, even by the standards of the high-end dinosaur market. And there's a good reason this particular specimen attracted so much attention.Why is this dinosaur skeleton so rare?Jodi is one of only three Nanotyrannus skeletons known to science, according to Sotheby's. Its skull is almost completely preserved, making it a particularly notable specimen.The mounted skeleton measures 19.6 feet from nose to tail and stands about 9.6 feet tall. It contains roughly 191 fossil bone elements, giving a sense of the scale of the work involved in recovering and assembling the remains.The story began in 2019, when Montana rancher Jodi Pierson discovered the fossil on her private land. The property sits within the Hell Creek Formation, an area famous for discoveries of prehistoric animals.Commercial paleontologist Clayton Phipps later led the excavation. Recovering a fossil of this size takes time and care, and the work of preserving the bones was essential to bringing the skeleton to its current form.The specimen was named after Pierson, whose discovery eventually led to one of the biggest dinosaur fossil sales in recent years.From a Montana ranch to a â¹449 crore auctionBefore the auction, Jodi was displayed in Manhattan, where visitors could get a closer look at the enormous skeleton.Sotheby's had expected it to fetch around $9 million, or approximately â¹85.5 crore. The final price of $47.3 million, equivalent to roughly â¹449 crore, was a very different story.The sale is among the most expensive ever recorded for a dinosaur fossil. It also marks the first time a Nanotyrannus specimen has entered the commercial market since the genus was formally confirmed in 2025, according to the supplied report.For collectors, rare fossils can be valuable for several reasons. A specimen that is unusually complete, well preserved and scientifically significant is far less common than the fragments typically found during excavations. Jodi has all three qualities, which may help explain the competition among bidders.Still, the final price was a long way above the original estimate. The 12-minute bidding contest shows just how much interest the fossil generated.Smaller than a T. rex, but still worth a fortuneNanotyrannus may share a family connection with Tyrannosaurus rex, but Jodi is much smaller than the giant dinosaur most people picture when they think of prehistoric predators.At 19.6 feet long, it measures a little over half the length of Gus, a Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton that reportedly sold for $50.1 million, or around â¹476 crore, in July.That puts Jodi's sale into perspective. It didn't break the reported T. rex record, but its final price was still extraordinary for a specimen of its kind.Nanotyrannus has also attracted attention from scientists studying the relationships between different tyrannosaurs. Its classification has been the subject of debate, making well-preserved specimens particularly interesting to researchers.The commercial interest in Jodi, however, doesn't automatically tell us what the fossil might contribute to future research. That will depend on how it is studied and whether researchers can access it.What happens to Jodi now?After the sale, Cassandra Hatton, Sotheby's vice-chair and worldwide head of science and natural history, praised the people involved in finding, excavating and preserving the fossil. She said their work had played a major part in bringing Jodi to this point.As for the buyer, there has been no public announcement about what comes next. The skeleton could eventually be displayed for visitors, or it could become part of a private collection. For now, its future remains uncertain.That matters because fossils like Jodi aren't just impressive objects to look at. They can also help scientists understand the animals that lived millions of years ago. Public access and opportunities for research can make a difference to how much people learn from such discoveries.A discovery that turned into a record-breaking paydayJodi's journey from a Montana ranch to a â¹449 crore auction is an unusual one, to say the least. A discovery made in 2019 has ended up attracting international attention and a price far beyond what the auction house initially expected.The money is certainly eye-catching. But the fossil's rarity, its remarkably preserved skull and the story behind its discovery are what make it stand out.Now that Jodi has a new owner, the big question is whether people will get another chance to see the skeleton up close.
